title: Draft a small utility enclosure
description: Educational drawing exercise for a 6 m by 4 m utility enclosure. Dimensions are illustrative and are not a construction design.
objectives: Set drawing units and draw accurately at full scale
guided: Create a new metric drawing. Record the units and layer naming convention in a note.
Draw a 6000 mm by 4000 mm outer rectangle and a 1000 mm opening centered on the south side. Use object snaps rather than approximate clicks.
Place walls, opening, dimensions, and notes on separate layers with distinct lineweights.
Add overall and opening dimensions, north arrow, title, and an educational-use note. Check the drawing at a plotted scale.
mistakes: Drawing in paper units instead of model units
Dimensions placed on a geometry layer
Text too small at plotted scale
brief: Prepare a clear concept drawing of a small utility enclosure for an internal design discussion. Establish sensible units, layers, dimensions, and annotations. The team needs an editable drawing and a readable PDF; verify scale and legibility yourself.
deliverables: Short note describing units and layer scheme
checklist: Layers separate geometry, dimensions, and notes
PDF title, scale, and educational-use note are legible
starter: All dimensions are provided in the instructions; no proprietary file is required.

title: Organize and annotate a concept site plan
description: A concept parcel exercise using an invented 60 m by 40 m lot; no survey or regulatory claim is implied.
guided: Draw a 60 m east-west by 40 m north-south parcel with an origin at its southwest corner.
Add an illustrative 18 m by 12 m building footprint centered at (30 m, 21 m), a 5 m wide access strip from the south edge, and three tree symbols as reusable blocks.
Label parcel, building, access, north direction, and all assumed dimensions. State that the parcel and offsets are fictional.
Use a layer naming scheme and prepare a plotted view with lineweight hierarchy.
mistakes: Presenting invented setbacks as legal requirements
brief: An internal concept team needs a site diagram for an invented rectangular parcel. Show a building footprint, access, and landscape symbols. Define your own reasonable graphic hierarchy and explain all assumptions; deliver an editable source and presentation PDF.
checklist: Blocks and layers are used consistently
Assumptions are visible in the PDF
starter: Fictional coordinates and dimensions appear in this challenge.

title: Prepare a drawing sheet for review
description: Turn an educational concept drawing into a readable review sheet, without implying issue-for-construction status.
guided: Use your enclosure or site-plan drawing as the model-space source.
Create an A3 or 11 x 17 inch layout with a simple original title block, drawing title, date, and revision marked Draft.
Create and lock a viewport at a documented scale. Set page setup, lineweights, and PDF output.
Review the PDF at 100% zoom for clipped labels, missing fonts, and readable dimensions.
mistakes: Plotting to an unexpected sheet size
brief: Prepare one clear review sheet from an educational CAD model. Choose an appropriate sheet size and scale, include document identification and draft status, and supply both editable source and PDF.
deliverables: Editable DWG or DXF with layout
checklist: Viewport scale is documented and locked
Title and draft status are shown

title: Import survey points and build existing ground
description: Create an educational existing-ground surface from a small fictional point set. It is not a real survey.
objectives: Import point data with correct columns and units
Create and inspect a TIN surface
Identify surface limits and possible bad triangles
guided: Create a CSV with columns Point, Easting, Northing, Elevation, Description using these rows: 1,0,0,101.2,EG; 2,50,0,101.8,EG; 3,100,0,102.6,EG; 4,0,50,100.9,EG; 5,50,50,101.5,EG; 6,100,50,102.1,EG; 7,0,100,100.4,EG; 8,50,100,101.0,EG; 9,100,100,101.7,EG. Values are metres in a local invented coordinate system.
Import with a matching point-file format. Confirm all nine points and elevations.
Build an existing-ground TIN, add an outer boundary around the 100 m square, and display contours at a sensible interval.
Inspect triangles and record two limits of this sparse, fictional dataset.
brief: An internal concept study has nine fictional elevation points in a local metre grid. Import them, create a bounded existing-ground TIN, and explain where interpolation is weak. Provide an editable model and a legible surface exhibit.
starter: The original nine-point CSV dataset is fully specified in the guided instructions.

title: Lay out an alignment and existing-ground profile
description: Create a conceptual route through the fictional surface; no roadway standard or approval is claimed.
guided: Use the nine-point educational surface from the survey challenge.
Create a centerline from (10,20) through (50,45) to (90,75) metres in the local grid. Add a reasonable curve for a concept exercise and document your chosen radius.
Set stationing from 0+000 and sample the existing-ground profile from the surface.
Create a profile view with legible station and elevation labels. Inspect where the route approaches the sparse surface boundary.
mistakes: Profile sampled from the wrong surface
brief: A concept team wants a preliminary route across the fictional terrain. Choose and document an alignment, derive the existing-ground profile, and provide a plan/profile exhibit that makes assumptions visible.
checklist: Profile is associated with the correct surface
Station and elevation labels are readable

title: Build a conceptual roadway corridor
description: Model a short educational corridor using invented geometry. It is not a design for construction or compliance review.
objectives: Create a design profile and simple assembly
guided: Continue the fictional alignment and existing-ground profile.
Create a simple design profile with a documented start elevation and mild grade; explain the choice rather than claiming a standard.
Create an assembly with two illustrative 3 m lanes and simple shoulders. Build a corridor along the alignment.
Generate three cross sections at documented stations and review daylight or target warnings. Report any unresolved geometry.
mistakes: Treating default assembly dimensions as standards
Omitting warnings from the review note
brief: Prepare a conceptual corridor model for an internal learning review. Select a simple cross section and profile, then show three representative sections and explain design assumptions and unresolved warnings.
checklist: All dimensions and warnings are labeled educational

title: Model a small two-room studio
description: Create an educational building model with invented dimensions, not a permit or construction model.
objectives: Model basic walls, floors, doors, and windows
Create views that explain the model
guided: Start a new model using your installed Revit templates. Set Level 1 at 0 m and Level 2 at 3 m.
Lay out a 10 m by 8 m rectangular studio with two rooms separated by an interior wall. Add a floor, one exterior door, one interior door, and two windows using available families.
Name rooms and views consistently. Create a Level 1 plan and a 3D view.
Check that doors open into intended spaces and that walls and floor align at their levels.
mistakes: Elements assigned to the wrong level
brief: An internal team needs a simple concept BIM model for an invented two-room studio. Organize levels, rooms, openings, and views so another modeler can understand the file. Document template and family assumptions.
checklist: Doors and windows appear in plan and 3D
starter: Dimensions and program are supplied here; use locally installed Revit templates and families.

title: Model an illustrative foundation layout
description: Practice structural BIM elements with fictional loads and dimensions. No structural adequacy is asserted.
guided: In a separate educational model or copy, define a 2 by 2 grid with 6 m spacing in each direction.
Place four structural columns at the grid intersections and four illustrative isolated footings using installed families. Choose dimensions solely for modeling practice.
Create a foundation plan and a schedule listing footing mark, type, and dimensions.
Annotate the drawing as educational and state that sizing requires an engineer and site-specific information.
mistakes: Architectural instead of structural column category
brief: Build a coordinated model of four columns and illustrative footings for a fictional concept. Organize grids, levels, and a footing schedule. Identify information required before any engineering design could be attempted.
checklist: Footings appear on the intended level
Schedule matches modeled elements and carries educational status

title: Produce a coordinated model documentation set
description: Prepare a small review set from an educational Revit model, without suggesting construction readiness.
guided: Use the two-room studio model or a fresh educational model of similar scope.
Create a Level 1 plan, one section through both rooms, and a door schedule with mark, type, and width.
Place views on two original review sheets. Include drawing title, date, and Draft / Educational status.
Check that door marks on the plan match the schedule and that section callouts resolve to the correct view.
mistakes: Schedule filtered to omit a door
Sheet annotations implying an issued design
brief: An internal reviewer needs a compact coordinated drawing set from an educational BIM model. Choose the most useful plan, section, and schedule views; resolve inconsistent tags and present two readable draft sheets.
deliverables: Door schedule PDF or included sheet
checklist: Both sheets are clearly draft educational material
